nodes.label: Sirry, 'Who Are Those in Authority?' (2021)
nodes.status: metadata_and_abstract_verified; full argument requires section-level review
nodes.role: peer-reviewed historical study of early Sunni and Shi'i tafsir

nodes.label: Sirry's study describes internal diversity and historical development
nodes.summary: Sirry's study traces interpretations of Q 4:59 and 4:83 in selected Sunni and Shi'i tafsir across the first six centuries of Islamic history, arguing that interpretation developed over time and that disagreement also occurred within each broad tradition.
nodes.locator: Abstract and Introduction, especially scope and stated argument; accessed 2026-10-14

nodes.label: Sirry's account of diversity in early exegesis
nodes.summary: Sirry argues that selected Sunni and Shi'i interpretations of ulū al-amr developed historically and that interpretive disagreement existed within both traditions.

nodes.summary: Seed workbook; bibliographic records remain to be verified.

nodes.label: Al-Tabari's preferred reading of ulū al-amr
nodes.summary: In his commentary on Q 4:59, al-Tabari prefers identifying ulū al-amr with rulers and those appointed over Muslims, whose commands are obeyed when they do not involve disobedience to God and serve communal welfare.

nodes.label: Al-Tabari, Jami' al-bayan, commentary on Q 4:59
nodes.role: classical tafsir; primary source for al-Tabari's interpretation

nodes.label: Al-Tabari surveys and selects readings of ulū al-amr
nodes.summary: Al-Tabari reports readings including commanders/rulers, scholars and jurists, Companions, and Abu Bakr and Umar. He selects rulers and those appointed over Muslims, with obedience limited to commands consistent with obedience to God and the community's welfare.
nodes.locator: Commentary on Q 4:59; paragraphs beginning 'واختلف أهل التأويل' and 'وأولى الأقوال' (online text, accessed 2026-10-14)

nodes.label: Al-Tabataba'i, Al-Mizan, commentary on Q 4:59
nodes.status: text_and_locator_verified; print edition details not yet verified
nodes.role: modern Twelver Shi'i tafsir in English translation; primary source for the author's interpretation

nodes.label: Al-Tabataba'i's Twelver reading of ulū al-amr
nodes.summary: Al-Tabataba'i argues that Q 4:59's unqualified command to obey ulū al-amr entails their protection from sin and error, and interprets them as the Imams.

nodes.label: Al-Tabataba'i argues that Q 4:59 implies infallible authority
nodes.summary: Al-Tabataba'i argues that because Q 4:59 commands obedience to the Messenger and those vested with authority without an explicit condition, the latter must be protected from sin and error; he identifies this reading with the Imams.
nodes.locator: Commentary 'O You Who Believe! Obey Allah And Obey The Messenger', especially argument at paragraphs 106-128 and conclusion at 279 (web text, accessed 2026-10-14)
